cards.title: Variables
cards.body: `const` creates a variable: a name for a value. Use the name later to get the value back.

hi.title: Variables
hi.body: `const` ek variable banata hai: kisi value ka naam. Baad mein woh naam likho aur value wapas mil jaayegi.

cards.title: Reading input with prompt()
cards.body: On Loophole, `prompt()` reads one line of input as text, just like `prompt()` asks the user for text in a browser.

hi.title: prompt() se input padhna
hi.body: Loophole par `prompt()` input ki ek line text ki tarah padhta hai, bilkul waise jaise browser mein `prompt()` user se text maangta hai.

cards.title: Dropping values into text
cards.body: A string between backticks (the key left of 1) can drop in values with `${...}`. It reads more easily than gluing pieces with `+`.

hi.title: Text mein values daalna
hi.body: Backticks (1 ke left wali key) ke beech ki string mein `${...}` se values daal sakte ho. Yeh `+` se tukde jodne se zyada aasaani se padha jaata hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: Type `Asha` and it prints `Hi, ${name}!` instead of `Hi, Asha!`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: Only backtick strings fill in `${name}`. Line 2 uses double quotes, so it prints the letters exactly as typed.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: `Asha` type karo toh yeh `Hi, Asha!` ki jagah `Hi, ${name}!` print karta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: Sirf backtick strings hi `${name}` bharti hain. Line 2 double quotes use karti hai, isliye letters bilkul waise hi print hote hain jaise type kiye.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Inside backticks, `${animal}` is replaced by the value of `animal`, which is "cat".

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Backticks ke andar `${animal}` ki jagah `animal` ki value aa jaati hai, jo "cat" hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a name and print `Hi, <name>!`. For `Ada`, print `Hi, Ada!`
exercise.promptHi: Ek naam padho aur `Hi, <name>!` print karo. `Ada` ke liye `Hi, Ada!` print karo.
